note: Config of tools/leakguard.py (the numeric-literal leak guard). The reference files are read in place from paths.local.json "refs" (rom, cart_program, sub_program) and "brain_dir" (the three brain files, md5s in fwbuild.json "brain"); a reference whose md5 differs stops the guard (exit 2). The allow-list is tools/leak_allow.json.

sources.why: C/H/S/py are the languages a table can be typed in; .ld and .json are scanned too (a table in a config is still a table). Docs (.md) are prose: their thousands separators make number runs of our own sizes; they are not scanned.

window.why: 8 consecutive values = 16 B as u16, 32 B as u32; as u8, 12 values = 12 B (measured: 8 u8 values of our own generated sfx8 curve equal 9 bytes of 8-bit PCM in the ROM by coincidence; smooth 8-byte stretches are common in 8 MB of samples). Windows with fewer than 5 different values, or whose steps take at most 2 values (ramps, staircases, a hex-digit string after a NUL pad), match any counter table and are skipped; so are windows of mostly zero bytes.

sections.why: Built ELF sections of every Pocket build: data sections (.rodata/.data/.sdata/.srodata) in 12-byte windows against every reference; code sections in 16-byte windows against the non-RV32 references only (the brain files are RV32 code too, and GCC's prologue/epilogue idioms match them by construction; a table typed into an assembler file is caught at the source). The brain's own bytes (.brain_irom, cf.bin and the image tables at the start of .wram_text) are linked from outside the tree and excluded after an exact byte check.
